title: Power Apps: calendar and card layouts for views in model-driven apps
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts and the related environment settings are supported, with no blocking findings. The licensing requirement is supported by the licensing FAQ, but the briefing should acknowledge the conflicting Environment Maker exception on Microsoft's app-sharing page. Embedded directions in the earlier verifier comment were ignored as historical material.

claims.claim: No Microsoft Learn configuration page identifying these new layouts was found at review.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Apps" "575294" "new view layout"; "model-driven" "calendar" "stack of cards". Opened app-designer-overview, create-edit-views, add-calendar-control, create-card-forms; results document existing calendar controls and legacy card forms, not this roadmap feature.

claims.claim: The feature is user-opt-in: makers choose the layouts in the designer, with no separate admin switch found.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps calendar card layouts model-driven apps enable disable environment tenant setting Power Platform API pac organization table. Read settings-features, pac env, organization and app-designer-overview; no layout switch found. Roadmap says makers choose and configure layouts.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Running model-driven apps requires a licence providing Power Apps premium use rights.
claims.quote: Every user who runs a model-driven app needs a license that provides Power Apps premium use rights.
claims.fix: Keep the FAQ requirement and add: "Microsoft's Share a model-driven app page separately says users assigned the Environment Maker security role don't require licences to use model-driven apps, which conflicts with the licensing FAQ." Link to https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/maker/model-driven-apps/share-model-driven-app#app-sharing-privilege-and-licensing-requirements, which states: "Users who have the Environment Maker security role assigned don't require licenses to use model-driven apps."

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Power Apps Premium is a general entitlement option satisfying the premium use-rights requirement.
claims.quote: While Power Apps Premium, Power Apps per app plans, and the Power Apps per app pay-as-you-go meter that give premium Power Apps usage rights satisfy the requirement generally, use rights differ by license and by the context the app runs in.

claims.claim: Environment grid and view settings are in Power Platform admin center at Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Grids and views.
claims.quote:
In the navigation pane, select **Manage**.
In the **Manage** pane, select **Environments**.
On the **Environments** page, select an environment.
In the command bar, select **Settings**.
Expand **Product**, and then select **Features**.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not tie advancedcolumneditorenabled to the new calendar and card layouts.
claims.quote: Searched: organization reference for advancedcolumneditorenabled, calendar, card and layout; "model-driven" "calendar" "layouts" "enable" "API". Read the organization's writable-column definition and pac env; the column describes display column options, with no new-layout connection.

claims.claim: No separate tenant or environment switch for the new calendar and card layouts is documented on either the admin UI or automation surface as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps calendar card layouts model-driven apps enable disable environment tenant setting Power Platform API pac organization table; "model-driven" "calendar" "layouts" "enable" "API". Read settings-features, pac env and organization; no separate switch found.
